purpose: Replace only the presenter identity while preserving the source frame, source prop copy, source overlay pixels, camera, timing, audio and action.
authorised_generated_pixels: presenter face within a per-frame face/head mask
only those connected hair/skin pixels needed to make the identity boundary physically plausible
locked_source_pixel_layers: plum long-sleeve source wardrobe outside the authorised mask
both hands and fingers unless a separately reviewed hand-repair mask is necessary
white cards, every handwritten character, paper edge and tear state
yellow Hindi response subtitle pixels and their source geometry
camera framing, source cut timing and source audio
layer_order_back_to_front: source hands when they overlap the card or face boundary
hard_acceptance_gates: A generated image must never be used as the complete scene plate.
Every protected layer is composited from decoded source pixels after the identity edit; it is not redrawn, OCR-retyped or prompt-described.
For every anchor, pixel comparison outside the union of its authorised mask and explicit alpha-feather boundary must pass; any changed protected pixel fails the anchor.
Every card/question and every yellow subtitle must be visually present and source-identical at its anchor; a blank card, altered word, mojibake or omitted subtitle fails the anchor.
The director storyboard may use only accepted replacement keyframes as scene cards. Its labels may be rendered in the margin, never by a scene-image generator.
No Seedance or other video-generation request may be created until the replacement-keyframe manifest and its QC records pass.
forbidden_shortcuts: text-to-image or image-to-image generation from a prose-only reverse script
asking an image model to recreate legible source card copy or subtitles
blank-card substitutions used to avoid typography errors
using source contact sheets as the sole visual reference while omitting their pixels from the final cards
submitting any superseded storyboard as a video reference
storyboard_definition: A deterministic director layout whose scene cards are the already accepted replacement keyframes. It is a review artifact, not a new scene-generation step.
